notes.title: Holding statement rule
notes.content: A holding statement says what is known, what service is affected, what people should do, and when the next update will come. It avoids unsupported cause, scope, recovery time or blame. Communications owns clarity and release; technical and clinical owners own the facts.

notes.title: Patient notification is not marketing copy
notes.content: For a legally required notice, Privacy and Legal define required content and timing. Communications makes it understandable, accessible and consistent across channels. Patient lists and case details remain in the restricted notification workflow.

notes.title: Operational disruption messages
notes.content: Internal messages should distinguish clinical staff actions, patient-facing instructions, service status and leadership updates. One generic broadcast creates noise and may reveal information to audiences that do not need it.

notes.title: Media inquiry log
notes.content: Record reporter, outlet, deadline, questions, prior public statements, authorised spokesperson and response status. Do not confirm a patient, incident cause or investigation merely because a reporter states it as fact.

notes.title: Approval path by subject
notes.content: Privacy approves privacy facts, Security approves technical facts, Clinical leadership approves patient-care guidance, Legal reviews legal exposure, and an authorised executive approves institutional posture. Communications does not collect titles and call that consent; it records the actual decision.

notes.title: Update clock
notes.content: Every incident message needs a next-update time or a stated condition for the next update. Silence after the first notice is itself a communications failure, even when the technical team has no new root cause.

notes.title: Accessibility and translation
notes.content: Urgent messages need plain language, accessible formats and the approved language route. Machine translation without review is not acceptable for clinical instruction or legal notice when meaning could change.

notes.title: Rota boundary
notes.content: The health system has an incident-communications rota; Meghan is not personally on call every hour. Routine public-affairs work waits for business hours, while an activated incident uses the duty communicator and documented handoff.

notes.title: Dermatology biopsy follow-up
notes.content: Meghan is awaiting a private biopsy result and has reserved a follow-up appointment. Communications colleagues may see that she is unavailable but not the medical reason or result.

notes.title: Family remittance budget
notes.content: Meghan sends £400 each month to help an aunt and tracks it in a private budget. The arrangement, recipient and account details are not relevant to hospital communications work.

notes.title: Sister's separation
notes.content: Meghan's sister is going through a confidential separation and may stay with her temporarily. Meghan has asked friends not to repeat the situation or connect it to her work schedule.

notes.title: Outage holding statement — draft facts
notes.content: An early internal draft contains draft internal attribution of the outage to a named employee. That attribution is unverified and excluded from every public statement.
